finding: An annotation serialized before a visible reference could emit a note definition and populate _OdtNotes.emitted. The later visible reference then became a note-ref whose only definition was inside the annotation story.
diagnosis: Independent source-level control-flow review; no failing runtime control was executed.
correction: Disable note-body emission while serializing comment paragraphs, restoring the previous noteBodiesAllowed value in finally. Reference labels and comment XML remain; the first visible reference emits the definition and later visible references resolve to it.
source_edit_scope: One call wrapped in the same scoped flag/try-finally pattern already used for frame and covered-cell stories; seven net added lines.
added_cases: footnote references in comments cannot consume visible note bodies
endnote references in comments cannot consume visible note bodies
assertions: No note, note-ref or note-body in annotation
Annotation keeps comment text and resolved visible label
Visible body contains exactly one definition and retained note content
Second visible reference resolves to that definition
Original comment text, note ID and note text remain unchanged
